about: The security class (controller ruling 2026-11-01, F7 (a)): a lane whose merge into develop changes a path matching a glob in `paths`, or a path holding a `tokens` word anywhere (case-folded), takes a cold Opus read before the familiar's --no-ff merge lands. The familiar asks from the landing bench, standing at develop: `node tools/cold-read-owed.mjs <lane-ref>` pins `refs/remotes/origin/develop` and the lane head once (a bench whose HEAD differs from that base, or a lane head equal to it, refuses), compares the two trees (`git diff-tree -r --no-renames --ignore-submodules=none --raw -z <base> <lane>`), adds the paths of the tree the merge itself would make (`git merge-tree --write-tree`; a conflict reads unread), and matches with this file and the matcher (packages/lararium-tw5/src/filters/security-class.ts) as develop's git objects hold them, never the lane's and never a daemon's. It prints `COLD READ OWED: <paths>` or `cold read: none owed`, a record hash over the head, the base, this file's sha256 and the owed paths, and the landing command naming the pinned head sha; a judge that cannot read answers `COLD READ OWED: (unread: <why>)`, never clean. The familiar records the read under that hash and quotes it in the merge message (`Cold-Read: <hash>`). After the merge and before the push, `node tools/cold-read-owed.mjs --check-merge HEAD <head-sha>` holds the merge to that base and that head and judges the merge's own tree again, so a lane that moved after the read or a hand's resolution cannot land unread. This file sits in its own list, and the judge reads unread wherever the list stops owing its own path. The code that decides CI's verdict (cells, shards, witnesses, the build stamp, every manifest and test config) sits in the class too. Prune from evidence; never widen a hole.
